note: Block catalogue for composable receipt strips. A strip is an ordered list of blocks; each block is its own bordered card on a three-column grid and small blocks share rows. Moods change only the look (ornament, icon, accent), never the size or the grid. Slot names reuse printarr's slot names where they exist (greeting, title, metrics, paragraph, tip).

margins.note: A strip carries no blank of its own. The blank before the cut (about 90 dots, half an inch) is fed with the cut command, once at the end of the whole piece.

strip_rules.print_trigger: per recipient, when they arrive or unplug, or on an explicit print-now request. Never a shared strip for two people.

greeting.label: Greeting

slots.summary: string, optional, one or two lines

greeting.renders: headline at scale 3, then the summary wrapped at body scale

metric.label: Metric tile
metric.units: 2 to 4 (a label can wrap to two lines, and a sparkline adds height)

slots.label: string
slots.range: string, optional, the time span of the sparkline (default 24H)

metric.renders: label, numeral at scale 3, unit, optional sparkline

metric_rows.label: Metric rows

slots.rows: list of {label, value, unit}, up to 6 rows

metric_rows.renders: label, dot leaders, value right-aligned at the card edge

graph.label: Graph

slots.title: string
slots.series: list of numbers, oldest first, up to 48
slots.range: string, optional, the time span such as 24H or 12H (default 24H)

graph.renders: line graph with HIGH and LOW above it, and the span and NOW under it

dog_counts.label: Dog counts

slots.dogs: list of {name, pee, poop, food, run} counts, up to 2

dog_counts.renders: one row per dog, counts in the four categories

message.label: Message
message.renders: header ornament, wrapped paragraph, divider ornament, sign-off

alert.label: Alert
alert.renders: filled pill with the label, paragraph, action row

checklist.label: Checklist
checklist.renders: box or tick sprite per item, text at body scale

tip.label: Tip
tip.renders: one line with a small icon

fact.label: Fun fact
fact.renders: playful header and divider, the fact, FUN FACT label

mood_rules: Moods change the ornament, icon and accent only. Size, grid, font and card shell never change. One ornament per card: the first of header or divider that the block draws. Footer ornaments are not used on cards.

block_type.greeting: Does this content open the message with a greeting to a person by name?
block_type.metric_tiles: Does this content give one or two numbers with a trend?
block_type.metric_rows: Does this content give a list of labelled values?
block_type.graph: Does this content describe a change over time?
block_type.dog_counts: Does this content count events for a dog?
block_type.message: Does this content read as a message from one person to another?
block_type.alert: Does this content warn about a problem at home?
block_type.checklist: Does this content list things to buy or do?
block_type.tip: Does this content give one piece of advice?
block_type.fact: Does this content share a fun fact?

mood.happy: Is the content positive and cheerful?
mood.excited: Is the content enthusiastic about something?
mood.loving: Does the content express love or affection?
mood.playful: Is the content light-hearted or joking?
mood.reminder: Is the content a reminder about a task or time?
mood.factual: Is the content plain information with no emotion?
mood.sad: Is the content sad or disappointed?
mood.confused: Is the content unsure, asking a question, or unclear?
mood.upset: Is the content angry or upset?
mood.gentle_warning: Is the content a calm heads-up about something to check?
mood.firm_complaint: Does the content complain and ask for a change?
mood.urgent: Does the content need action right away?

grid_rules.card_width: 1, 2 or 3 columns; 3 is the full paper width
grid_rules.card_height: whole units; unit = 40 dots; card = units*40 - 10
grid_rules.fluid: text blocks measure their content and take the units it needs, within min_units and max_units
grid_rules.overflow: a fluid card past max_units is shortened at the end of its text and marked with ...
grid_rules.packing: consecutive blocks share a row while their spans add up to 3 or less
grid_rules.row_height: all cards in a row take the tallest card's units
grid_rules.text_min_span: text blocks need at least 2 columns
